interpretations.rationale: This experiment asserts the defect and its repair, and every declared predicate held. Admission index 0 records the fixture (no snapshots on A, ten committed commands, A holding {A,B,C}). Isolated for a second the node knows no leader and refuses the outside candidate P while it holds three configured servers (comparison 0, index 1). After the restart with the feature it reports no servers at all with last applied 13 (index 2), never campaigns under isolation, and grants the identical probe while adopting its term (comparison 1, index 3). When it is put back in contact and the leader appends one ordinary configuration entry for a new member D, the node's own configuration becomes {A,B,C,D} and it holds the new member (comparison 2, index 4) although its snapshot store is still empty, so the entry must have arrived through the AppendEntries configuration path. Isolated again it refuses the identical probe with the candidate outside that configuration and no leader known (comparisons 3 and 4, index 5).
counterevidence: The node's configuration is refilled by ordinary replication rather than by the restart, so the empty configuration is a bounded window rather than a permanent state.
The node never campaigns while its configuration is empty, so the defect is the vote it grants and not a stray candidacy of its own.
The grant and the refusal are produced by the same probe against the same node, so the difference is the configuration rather than the request or the node.
limitations: The configuration change was issued by the harness on the node that was leader and its future reported 'leadership lost while committing log', so the entry was committed under a leadership change rather than in one uninterrupted term; the refill of the node's own configuration is nonetheless read from the node itself.
The added member D has no stores or transport and never votes, so the change committed without it.
The installSnapshot repair path is not exercised; only the AppendEntries configuration path is.
Single sample per phase with in-memory stores and transports at scaled 50ms timeouts, each isolation window being one second.

interpretations.rationale: Answer: a node restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs while it holds no snapshot comes up with an empty configuration; that empty configuration is not inert, because the node still grants its vote to candidates it cannot see and that vote is enough to elect a leader its own committed configuration excludes; the window ends as soon as an ordinary configuration entry reaches it. Receipts bdf2837a4c004f95b6c9b19db4fb8154 (the two restarts: empty with the feature, {A,B,C} without it) and d2973ec8cc524a9089c63dd046e1a4ff (the same restarts under isolation: no campaigning with the empty configuration, candidate state for the control) establish the configuration outcome and the election gate. Receipt 1fb8595fb8664713a0dff87236bde04a adds the admission side: the node refuses the outside candidacy while it holds {A,B,C} (index 2) and grants the identical request once the restart has left it with no servers (index 4), after which an outside node whose log records {A,X} reaches leader state with the emptied node as its only voter partner while the node's log still commits {A,B,C} and the cluster's leader keeps its leadership (index 5). Receipt 6421d22975164b049baf3e8fc18529d2 adds the repair: the same node, reconnected, adopts the configuration {A,B,C,D} from one ordinary replicated configuration entry (index 4) even though its snapshot store is still empty, and the identical probe is then refused again with the candidate outside that configuration and no leader known (index 5). Mechanism: the scan starting at max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 combined with the replay that raises lastApplied past the configuration entry leaves latest empty, the election gate blocks campaigning while latestIndex is zero (raft.go 225-246), the membership guard in requestVote is conditional on a non-empty server list (raft.go 1656-1680), and r.configurations is refilled only by the AppendEntries configuration path or an installSnapshot. Bounds: the vote is still constrained by the log up-to-dateness rule and by the candidate's own quorum, so the defect yields one decisive grant rather than open admission, and it lasts only until a configuration entry or snapshot reaches the node.
counterevidence: The control restart without the feature rebuilds {A,B,C} and does campaign, so the empty configuration is not a property of the stores or of the restart procedure.
The node's FSM replayed the log to index 13 in the restart and probe receipts, so missing entries do not explain the empty configuration.
The emptied node never becomes a candidate, so the containment argument still holds; the defect is the vote it grants, not a stray candidacy of its own.
The empty configuration ends at the first replicated configuration entry, and the same probe is refused afterwards, so the authority it granted is bounded by repair timing.
limitations: The empty configuration is observed at construction and after a 300ms settle; the absence of snapshots is arranged by the harness (ten-minute interval, none taken) rather than caused by a store failure.
The outsider's stores are supplied by the harness, so the scenario models a node whose recorded configuration {A,X} was never this cluster's.
The probes are hand-built vote requests and the two sides stay partitioned, so no write conflict between the two leaders is executed.
The repair used one harness-issued configuration change whose future reported a leadership change while committing, and the installSnapshot repair path was not exercised.
interpretations.joint_history: Four receipts of four experiments on this question. bdf2837a4c004f95b6c9b19db4fb8154 records the two restarts and the configuration each produces (empty with the feature, {A,B,C} without it); d2973ec8cc524a9089c63dd046e1a4ff is the revision of that same harness that adds the isolation phase and records whether the restarted node campaigns; 1fb8595fb8664713a0dff87236bde04a is an independent harness that repeats the fixture, the feature-enabled restart and the isolation, then probes the node's vote admission and runs a real outside candidate against it; 6421d22975164b049baf3e8fc18529d2 repeats the same fixture, restart and probes and then adds the configuration-entry repair phase. They are compatible because all four observe the same cluster identity {A,B,C}, the same restart procedure from A's own stores with the feature on and off, and the same two resulting configurations; each receipt repeats the fixture rather than inheriting it, every comparison outcome is read from its own receipt, and the empty-configuration events of the third and fourth receipts (no servers, last applied 13) match the configuration recorded by the first two.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: when Config.RestoreCommittedLogs is enabled and the log store's persisted commit index covers a committed configuration entry newer than the node's last snapshot, NewRaft does not rebuild the node's configuration from that entry. restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go 724-753) reads the persisted commit index and calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil); processLogs advances lastApplied to that index (raft.go 1361-1362); the configuration scan then starts at max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 = commit+1 (api.go 610-620), so index 6 of the fixture - a committed LogConfiguration{A,B,C,D,E} that the node stores and that the FSM is asked to apply - is never passed to processConfigurationLogEntry. The node therefore keeps the snapshot's membership {A,B,C} in both r.configurations.latest and r.configurations.committed (latest index 1). Because a candidate's threshold and a node's voter set come only from configurations.latest (raft.go 313-320, 1085-1096) and vote requests are admitted based on the receiver's configuration (raft.go 1660-1680), the restarted node's election quorum is 2 instead of 3. The condition is not self-healing in the observed paths: duplicate entries are skipped before processConfigurationLogEntry (raft.go 1526-1553), so a leader that already has this follower's log matched does not cause the entry to be re-processed, and the configurations are only refreshed by new entries or by an installed snapshot (raft.go 1955-1962). Local construction feedback on the draft harness returned exactly the predicted difference (feature off: lastApplied 5, latest {A,B,C,D,E} at index 6, quorum 3; feature on: lastApplied 7, latest {A,B,C} at index 1, quorum 2, and the live case reporting {A,B,C} through GetConfiguration); the retained execution is the basis for changing this account, so the account is conditional on the filed experiment's receipt. Counterevidence and limits: the fixture's log and snapshot indexes are supplied rather than produced by a live node, the multi-node election with a minority of the true configuration was not executed, and the node still stores the newer configuration entry in its log (so a reviewer may argue repair is possible through a later entry or an installed snapshot); the abandoned-write consequence therefore stays a source-reasoned consequence until a multi-node witness exists. The second registered question (constructor replay backpressure) is independent of this account.
counterevidence: The node does store the newer committed configuration entry in its log (the FSM batch is queued for index 6/7), so the stale membership is not a missing entry but an unprocessed one.

interpretations.rationale: The predicates declared for this cluster are contradicted by valid witnesses. Admission index 0 establishes the setup: snapshot index 6 with configuration {A,B,C}, committed configuration entry at index 8 with {A,B,C,D,E}, stored commit index 8 covering that entry, and A reporting the five-voter membership before the restart. After A is restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs from its own stores (index 1) it reports {A,B,C} with last_applied 8, i.e. it holds the committed five-voter entry in its log and still uses the three-voter membership. With the partition {A,C} | {B,D,E} (index 2): A is Leader in the two-voter partition (stale_config_node_is_leader true, minority_leaders A, terms A:3,C:3), B is Leader on the other side (majority_leaders B, terms B:3,D:3,E:3), so leader_count is 2 rather than 1; both leaders accept and commit a command (minority_write_committed true, majority_write_committed by the same operand on the other side), and both commit at index 11 in term 3 with different payloads (minority_write_data minority-write, majority_write_data majority-write, conflicting_commits true). The in-partition control holds: C, whose configuration is the current one, never becomes leader in the same two-voter partition (index 2, comparison 5 holds), which is the expected behaviour when the quorum is three, and the rest of the cluster still reports {A,B,C,D,E} (comparison 6 holds), so the two sides lead with different membership views. Mechanism: the restart keeps the snapshot membership (api.go 610-620 with the replay from api.go 724-753 advancing lastApplied), the candidate threshold and voter set come from configurations.latest (raft.go 313-320, 1085-1096), and voters grant from their own configuration (raft.go 1660-1680), so two votes suffice where the current membership requires three; the persisted commit index that drives the replay only exists because the deployment ran with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled (raft.go 1393-1403). Limits: the control used here is the in-partition sibling with the correct configuration, not a no-feature restart of the same node, so the file's original control variant is unexecuted; A is shut down gracefully rather than crashed and only in-memory stores are used; the partition is transport-only and lasts for the observation window, so the later loss of the minority entry after healing is not observed.
counterevidence: C, in the same partition with the current configuration, cannot win because it needs three votes, which confirms the election difference comes from the configuration view and not from the partition alone.

interpretations.rationale: Answer: yes. A node left with a stale configuration by the RestoreCommittedLogs replay does win an election with fewer votes than the configuration recorded in its own committed log, and the rest of the cluster elects its own leader at the same time. Receipt b68f3d3a08b34cd6a27b76faeb0d2a3e shows the whole chain on stores produced by normal operations: the config entry at index 8 (five voters) is committed and stored while node A's snapshot stays at index 6 (three voters) and A's stored commit index is 8, the restarted A reports {A,B,C}, the partition {A,C} | {B,D,E} leaves A leader of two voters against a quorum of three and B leader of the other three, and both leaders commit a different entry at index 11 in term 3. The mechanism is the parent question's defect plus the quorum rule: candidate threshold and voter set come from configurations.latest (raft.go 313-320, 1085-1096) while voters admit requests from their own view (raft.go 1660-1680), so the stale node needs two votes where three are required. Scope: the witness is one cluster, one partition window and in-memory stores with a graceful shutdown rather than a crash; the no-feature restart control variant of the discriminator was replaced by the in-partition sibling with the correct configuration, which cannot lead for the same partition. Also open: whether the minority entry is dropped once the partition heals, and how long a stale node can keep acting as leader while it can still reach a stale majority.
counterevidence: The control sibling C in the same partition never leads, so the partition alone does not explain the leadership change.
The stale node's log is complete and committed up to index 8, so its election is not explained by a lagging log.
limitations: Single cluster, single partition window, in-memory stores and a graceful shutdown rather than a crash.
The intended no-feature restart control is unexecuted; the in-partition sibling stands in for it.
Post-healing fate of the conflicting entry at index 11 term 3 is not observed.

interpretations.rationale: This experiment asserts the defect and every declared predicate held. The fixture admission carries A with no snapshots, ten committed commands and the live configuration {A,B,C} (index 0). While A still holds that configuration and knows no leader, the probe sent on behalf of identity P - absent from the configuration - is refused (comparison 0, index 2), and the refusal is attributable to membership rather than to timing or log age, because the request carried a term one above A's and a last log entry equal to A's and the event records that no leader was known (comparison 1). After the restart with the feature, A reports no servers while its log still records {A,B,C} and its last applied index is 13 (index 3); isolated again it still never campaigns, and the identical probe is now granted with A adopting the probe term (comparison 2, index 4). The real outside node X, whose log is a copy of A's with the bootstrap configuration entry replaced by {A,X}, then reaches leader state with A as its only voter partner (comparison 3), A follows it (comparison 4), A's log still names the committed {A,B,C} (comparison 5) and the cluster's own leader B keeps its leadership at the same time (comparison 6), all read at index 5.
counterevidence: A's own election gate still refuses to campaign while its configuration is empty, so the node never becomes a candidate itself; the defect is in the authority it grants, not in its own transition.

The grant is not explained by the node's state: in the control the node was a candidate and refused, and the node that granted was a follower, so the two outcomes differ with the configuration rather than with the state.
The outsider needs a reachable voter partner: with X's configuration {A,X} its quorum is two, so the election is only completed because the emptied node supplies the second vote.
limitations: The outsider's stores are supplied by the harness, so the scenario models a node whose stored configuration {A,X} was never this cluster's; the same reachability arises for a server reinstated from an older deployment or a recycled address.
Single sample per phase with in-memory transports and stores at scaled 50ms timeouts; each isolation window is 1.2s, twenty heartbeat timeouts, and the state is sampled every 5ms.
The two sides stay partitioned during the probes, so no write is applied by both leaders and the concurrent-commit consequence is not executed here.
Both probes are hand-built vote requests carrying the target's own last log entry, so they test the admission branch rather than what an out-of-date candidate would experience.

interpretations.rationale: Answer: a node restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs while it holds no snapshot comes up with an empty configuration, and that empty configuration is not merely inert - the node refuses to campaign itself but still grants its vote to candidates it cannot see, which is enough to elect a leader its own committed configuration excludes. Receipts bdf2837a4c004f95b6c9b19db4fb8154 (the two restarts: empty with the feature, {A,B,C} without it) and d2973ec8cc524a9089c63dd046e1a4ff (the same restarts under isolation: no campaigning with the empty configuration, candidate state for the control) establish the configuration outcome and the gate. Receipt 1fb8595fb8664713a0dff87236bde04a adds the admission side: the same node, isolated and knowing no leader, refuses the outside candidacy while it holds {A,B,C} (index 2) and grants the identical request once the restart has left it with no servers (index 4); the outside node X, whose log records {A,X} and whose only voter partner is the emptied node, then reaches leader state at term 5 while the emptied node follows it with its log still committing {A,B,C} and the cluster's leader B keeps its leadership (index 5). Mechanism: the scan starting at max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 combined with the replay that raises lastApplied past the configuration entry leaves latest empty, the election gate then blocks campaigning while latestIndex is zero (raft.go 225-246), and the membership guard in requestVote is conditional on a non-empty server list (raft.go 1656-1680), so the emptied node admits and grants a vote it would otherwise refuse. Scope of the consequence: the vote is bounded by the log up-to-dateness rule and by the candidate's own quorum, so the defect yields one extra authority grant rather than unrestricted admission, and the node's participation resumes as soon as the cluster installs a snapshot or a configuration entry reaches it.

045d23497a8a47e79cccfb8361d0d6b9-gap-0.explanation: Yes to both. Receipt 1fb8595fb8664713a0dff87236bde04a executes the grant: the node with the empty configuration (configured_servers 0, last applied 13, no leader known) returns a granted vote to identity P, which appears in no configuration the node holds, whereas the same node holding {A,B,C} refuses the identical request (index 2 versus index 4, same probe term, same last log entry, no leader in either case). The grant is then enough to elect an outsider: node X, whose stores record the configuration {A,X} and whose only voter partner is the emptied node, reaches leader state at term 5, the emptied node follows it as a follower, and the cluster's own leader B keeps its leadership at the same time, so the election produced two leaders and one of them is absent from the configuration recorded in the node's own committed log (index 5). The practical bound is that the outsider still needs a reachable voter partner and an at-least-as-up-to-date log, so the defect supplies the deciding vote rather than open admission.

counterevidence: The control restart without the feature rebuilds {A,B,C} and does campaign, so the empty configuration is not a property of the stores or of the restart procedure.
The node's FSM replayed the log to index 13 in both the restart and the probe receipt, so missing entries do not explain the empty configuration.
The emptied node never becomes a candidate, so the containment argument still holds; the defect is the vote it grants, not a stray candidacy of its own.
The outside candidate is refused the moment the node holds the committed membership again, so the grant is a function of the empty configuration rather than of the node or the request.
limitations: The empty configuration is observed at construction and after a 300ms settle; the absence of snapshots is arranged by the harness (ten-minute interval, none taken) rather than caused by a store failure.
The outsider's stores are supplied by the harness, so the scenario models a node whose recorded configuration {A,X} was never this cluster's.
The probes are hand-built vote requests and the two sides stay partitioned, so no write conflict between the two leaders is executed.
In-memory stores and transports with scaled timeouts; one run per mode.

interpretations.rationale: This experiment asserts the defect and its repair, and every declared predicate held. Admission index 0 records the fixture (no snapshots on A, ten committed commands, A holding {A,B,C}). Isolated for a second the node knows no leader and refuses the outside candidate P while it holds three configured servers (comparison 0, index 1). After the restart with the feature it reports no servers at all with last applied 13 (index 2), never campaigns under isolation, and grants the identical probe while adopting its term (comparison 1, index 3). When it is put back in contact and the leader appends one ordinary configuration entry for a new member D, the node's own configuration becomes {A,B,C,D} and it holds the new member (comparison 2, index 4) although its snapshot store is still empty, so the entry must have arrived through the AppendEntries configuration path. Isolated again it refuses the identical probe with the candidate outside that configuration and no leader known (comparisons 3 and 4, index 5).
counterevidence: The node's configuration is refilled by ordinary replication rather than by the restart, so the empty configuration is a bounded window rather than a permanent state.
The node never campaigns while its configuration is empty, so the defect is the vote it grants and not a stray candidacy of its own.
The grant and the refusal are produced by the same probe against the same node, so the difference is the configuration rather than the request or the node.
limitations: The configuration change was issued by the harness on the node that was leader and its future reported 'leadership lost while committing log', so the entry was committed under a leadership change rather than in one uninterrupted term; the refill of the node's own configuration is nonetheless read from the node itself.
The added member D has no stores or transport and never votes, so the change committed without it.
The installSnapshot repair path is not exercised; only the AppendEntries configuration path is.
Single sample per phase with in-memory stores and transports at scaled 50ms timeouts, each isolation window being one second.
